page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-24GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 4 shared vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 24.0 GB of RAM, providing 6.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present.

Performance benchmarks indicate a shared-resource profile. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is in the bottom 10% at 780.79, while multi-core performance is in the bottom 25% at 3123.05. Memory performance is mixed; cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 411.67 GB/sec, but uncached large-block read bandwidth drops to a weak 36.0 GB/sec. PassMark CPU and extended instruction tests score in the average range, though the PassMark memory score is poor. Database operations and Redis SET operations both perform in the bottom 25%, reflecting the shared CPU allocation.

Given its shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage, this server offers a budget-friendly resource density for memory-leaning workloads that do not require sustained, high-performance compute. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for development environments, lightweight web serving, and basic background tasks. Appropriate workloads include non-critical CI/CD pipelines, staging environments, and small-scale applications where resource sharing does not impact core operations.
